title: AI as a transforming assemblage
doc: A contextual map of sticky notes on a pinboard. Edited at the encyclopedia's /sticky-map (three.js) and drawn in VR by commons/artifacts/sticky_map/sticky_map.gd with the same layout rules; positions are metres on the board, x across from its centre, y up from the floor. Links marked by:"proposed" are an organisation offered for revision, not part of the source text.

notes.title: The central argument
notes.short: AI is part of a continuously transforming assemblage of algorithms, human histories, material dependencies, institutions, labor and desire.
notes.body:
AI is not simply a tool, a threat, or an autonomous intelligence. It is part of a continuously transforming assemblage of algorithms, human histories, material dependencies, institutions, labor and desire.

As computational capabilities accelerate, critique cannot remain a fixed external judgment. It must become a situated, recursive practice that investigates and transforms the conditions under which intelligence, agency and value are produced.

The challenge is not merely to make AI more efficient or aligned with existing values, but to build communities capable of collectively sustaining, questioning and transforming those values and their technological conditions.

notes.title: 1 · World thickness
notes.short: Reality resists: computational, material, historical, political.
notes.body: Reality contains computational, material, historical and political resistance. Intelligence cannot simply optimize this complexity away. Thickness can protect democratic plurality but also preserve domination.

notes.title: 2 · Computability and P ≠ NP
notes.short: Finding, verifying and deciding what counts are distinct problems.
notes.body: Finding an answer, verifying an answer and deciding what counts as an acceptable answer are distinct problems. P ≠ NP concerns formal computational complexity, not whether reality is fundamentally algorithmic.

notes.title: 3 · Intelligence as a gradient
notes.short: Continuous representations of discrete language; meaning is not gradient optimization.
notes.body: LLMs learn through continuous-valued mathematical representations of discrete language. This suggests ways of thinking about changing relationships, but meaning and political legitimacy cannot be reduced to gradient optimization.

notes.title: 4 · Recursive critique
notes.short: Critique of the rules, constraints, objectives and evaluation, not only the state.
notes.body: Critique must investigate not only the state of a system but also its rules, constraints, objectives and evaluation criteria. It participates in the transformation of the assemblage.

notes.title: 5 · Algorithmic–VR–real
notes.short: Algorithms construct possibility; VR makes it experiential; the world shows consequences.
notes.body: Algorithms construct possibility spaces; VR makes them experiential; the sociotechnical world reveals histories and consequences. Observations and critique feed back into the construction.

notes.title: 6 · Power and the default
notes.short: Corporate values, training, infrastructure and domination shape AI.
notes.body: Paola's polyphonic priming ecology exposes how corporate values, training, infrastructure and histories of domination shape AI. Responsibility can become obscured across these layers.

notes.title: 7 · Labor, desire and reproduction
notes.short: The work and dependencies that sustain systems, inherited by the agents.
notes.body: Federici directs attention toward the work and dependencies sustaining systems. The Void Tower's agents inherit human labor and desire, even after humans disappear. Their purposes and possible collective organization remain open questions.

notes.title: 8 · The minus operation
notes.short: Subtract the dominant classification; see what remains. It traverses the map.
notes.body:
Porn minus porn, money minus money, identity minus its function as a credential. Subtracting a dominant classification or objective reveals residual dependencies and unexplored possibilities without erasing their histories.

The minus operation traverses the map: it questions inherited objectives and classifications at every level.

notes.title: 9 · Anticipatory commoning
notes.short: Shared infrastructures, agency, care and revisable governance under changing AI.
notes.body: Drawing on Articipation, we ask how communities can develop shared infrastructures, agency, maintenance, care and revisable governance under rapidly changing AI capabilities.

notes.title: Articipation 2012–2015
notes.short: Participation in network society: piracy, hackers, capture, commons.
notes.body: Articipation (2012–2015) investigated the conditions of participation in network society: piracy, hacker culture, institutional capture, alternative infrastructures, collective knowledge and the commons.

notes.title: Ada Research 2024–2026
notes.short: Generative algorithmic systems through VR worlds, grammars and AI-assisted construction.
notes.body: Ada Research (2024–2026) investigates the generative and transformative capacities of algorithmic systems through experimental VR worlds, computational grammars and AI-assisted construction.

notes.title: The emerging question 2026–
notes.short: Collective agency, critique and reproduction in AI-mediated environments.
notes.body:
The emerging question (2026 onward) is how collective agency, critique and social reproduction might be sustained within rapidly changing environments increasingly mediated by artificial intelligence.

There is continuity, but also a genuine development. The earlier question concerned how people participate in technological systems. Now we must also ask what participation means when artificial agents can act, generate and reorganize these systems.

notes.title: Where the Void Tower enters
notes.short: Agents in the residue of civilization; their activities become research problems.
notes.body:
The Void Tower gives the discussion an experimental and narrative form.

Its artificial agents inhabit the residue of human civilization. Labor, desire, hierarchy and procedural objectives remain encoded in the environment after the humans have disappeared.

We don't necessarily know whether these agents are workers in the human sense, whether they desire anything, or what their activities mean. Rather than answering those questions in advance, the world allows them to become research problems.

The player encounters the agents, investigates the procedures, changes rules and observes consequences. The world's inhabitants may also become capable of collectively changing their inherited conditions.

This is where assemblage becomes critique through transformation, and where critique has to confront reproduction: how the world and its inhabitants continue to exist.

notes.title: Computational
notes.short: The limits of algorithmic intelligence; what continuous representations say about meaning.
notes.body: What are the limits of algorithmic intelligence, and what can its continuous representations tell us about meaning and the world?

notes.title: Political
notes.short: Critique when AI absorbs, adapts to and commercializes its own criticism.
notes.body: How can critique remain effective when AI systems can rapidly absorb, adapt to and commercialize their own criticism?

notes.title: Ethical
notes.short: Intelligence, desire and agency without imposing human categories at once.
notes.body: Can we investigate forms of intelligence, desire and agency without immediately imposing human categories upon them?

notes.title: Collective
notes.short: Communities that sustain themselves, keep autonomy and transform their own rules.
notes.body:
How do we construct communities capable of sustaining themselves, preserving autonomy and transforming their own rules under accelerating technological change?

These four questions are connected, but I would resist collapsing them into one theory. Their tensions are productive.

notes.title: The next research proposition
notes.short: Intelligence and collective organization that transform the world without eliminating its differences.
notes.body: How can we develop forms of intelligence and collective organization that increase our capacity to transform the world without eliminating the differences, dependencies and resistances that make meaningful transformation possible?

notes.title: What this map is for
notes.short: Not an archive: a knowledge assemblage still open to transformation.
notes.body:
It should not merely archive our AI discussion. It should let us reorganize its arguments spatially, inspect their relationships, reveal contradictions, and unfold each concept into its full history and meaning.

In that sense, the contextual map would itself become an experiment in recursive critique: a knowledge assemblage whose organization remains available for transformation.
